categories.label: People, organizations, places, or systems involved

summary.title: Understand the operational need before defining the solution.
summary.body: Operational Analysis focuses on customer goals, expected missions and activities, real operational use, actors or users, operating conditions and constraints.

oa_help.details_label: Learn more about this Arcadia viewpoint

sections.title: Purpose
sections.body: Build a shared, solution-independent understanding of the operational problem and customer need. Describe the operational environment and expected outcomes before assigning responsibilities to the system.

sections.title: What to capture
items: People, roles, organizations and other operational entities
Operational scenarios and significant operating conditions
Constraints and dimensioning parameters such as safety, security, lifecycle, time, distance or capacity

sections.title: Questions to ask
items: Who or what participates in the operation?
What activities are performed, and by whom?
What information, material or requests are exchanged?
Which scenarios represent important operational use?
Which conditions, limits or constraints can change the expected outcome?

sections.title: Practical starting point
sections.body: A useful way to begin is to describe the operational story in plain language: who is involved, what they are trying to achieve, what happens, what is exchanged and which conditions matter. Formalize the model as that shared understanding becomes clear.

sections.title: What not to do yet
sections.body: Avoid defining the internal solution architecture too early. In Arcadia, the system contribution and boundary are addressed in System Analysis; Logical and Physical Architecture then develop the solution progressively.

sections.title: Arcadia perspective path
sections.body: The perspectives have methodological dependencies, but Arcadia is inherently iterative and can be applied incrementally, top-down, bottom-up or through reuse-driven approaches.

path.label: Operational Analysis
path.description: What users and operational stakeholders need to do.

path.label: System Analysis
path.description: What the system must achieve for them, including its boundary and external interactions.

path.label: Logical Architecture
path.description: A technology-neutral or notional decomposition of the solution.

path.label: Physical Architecture
path.description: How the solution is realized with physical, software, hardware or firmware components.

oa_help.source_note: Based on the official Arcadia and Capella method documentation.
